title: How to plan and book a successful trip to Workday Rising 2026
summary: Plan for Workday Rising 2026 at The Venetian. Explore Strip hotels, Expo strategy, Braindates, and how to make four days in Vegas count.
body_text: Key takeaways Workday Rising 2026 runs Oct. 12–15 at The Venetian Resort and Caesars Forum in Las Vegas. This guide walks through Strip hotels, LAS transfers, GSA budgeting, Expo strategy, and departure logistics for the four-day program. Compare hotel availability on The Venetian campus, central Strip properties, and north Strip options before you default to the closest or cheapest room rate. Conference-week Strip rates often run well above the federal per diem lodging rate, so budget for the gap or book through Workday's official housing portal. Navan Edge coordinates flights, hotels, and restaurant reservations in one chat when Rising room blocks fill up or there's less availability near The Venetian. Choose high-priority breakouts and preserve white space for Expo demos, Braindates, and Hands-On Labs. Send follow-up notes within two business days while product demos and tenant questions are still fresh. For four days in mid-October, Workday Rising 2026 will bring HR, finance, and IT leaders to Las Vegas for keynotes, product sessions, hands-on learning, and conversations with peers and Workday experts.[1] The choices you make before the conference, including where you stay and how you structure your agenda, will shape what you take home from Workday Rising. With a thoughtful plan, you can return with clearer priorities, stronger professional connections, and practical next steps. What is Workday Rising and who is it for? Workday Rising is Workday's flagship U.S. conference for human capital management (HCM), finance, and IT leaders exploring cloud ERP, analytics, and AI on the Workday platform.[1] The event runs Oct. 12–15 at The Venetian Resort and Caesars Forum in Las Vegas.[1][2] The conference typically attracts around 30,000 attendees, bringing together executives and practitioners from across the Workday ecosystem.[3] Expect to see CHROs and HRIS directors planning workforce and talent strategy, CFOs and controllers evaluating financial close and planning modules, CIOs and integration leads assessing platform extensibility, and partner teams supporting customer deployments. Workday Rising welcomes existing customers as well as invited prospects, sponsors, analysts, and accredited media.[3] The Workday Rising 2026 Session Catalog is live, with hundreds of sessions available to browse before the conference.[18] You can finalize your agenda and reserve eligible sessions in September once the Session Scheduler opens. If you're building the business case for attending, identify the outcomes you want to achieve before you arrive — whether that's evaluating new AI capabilities, comparing partner solutions, or meeting with peers to validate your roadmap. What makes Workday Rising 2026 worth the trip Workday Rising is where the company's product direction meets the practitioners who run it daily — not a replay of release notes you could read online. For HR and finance leaders, that means keynotes, roadmap sessions, and customer-led stories you can take back to your steering committee. For technical teams, it means Hands-On Labs and Express Labs where you test features in a guided tenant environment.[1][3][6] Some of the highest-value experiences happen outside the breakout rooms: Workday Rising Expo: Explore partner booths, product demonstrations, and sponsor exhibits throughout the Venetian Expo Center. Keynotes and product strategy sessions: Hear Workday executives share product updates, customer stories, and the company's long-term vision for HCM, Financial Management, and AI. Braindates: Join peer-led conversations to exchange ideas and learn how other organizations are approaching similar challenges. Hands-On Labs and Express Labs: Test new features in guided and self-paced technical environments with support from Workday experts. Welcome Reception: Connect with other attendees over drinks and light refreshments on Monday evening. Customer Appreciation Party: Continue networking at Wednesday's evening event with food, drinks, and entertainment. Official hotel shuttles: Take advantage of complimentary transportation between participating conference hotels and the Venetian Expo Center. The value of Workday Rising comes from what happens after the conference. A clear plan, stronger relationships with partners and peers, and answers to your biggest questions can all help move projects forward once you're back at work. Planning your travel, agenda, and meetings before you arrive makes it much easier to spend your time on those outcomes instead of conference logistics. Where to stay for Workday Rising 2026 Your hotel can impact more than where you sleep. It also determines how long you'll spend getting to the Venetian Expo Center, whether you can take a break between sessions, and how easily you can stay for evening networking events without worrying about a long trip back to your room. Workday negotiates discounted rates at 15 hotels near the Venetian Expo Center, and hotel reservations through the event portal close Tuesday, Sept. 29, 2026.[3] Hotels by distance to The Venetian Resort Compare these areas by walk time, atmosphere, and what you can typically expect to pay during Workday Rising week: Area Distance to venue Details Rates Venetian/Palazzo campus 0–5 minutes walking (indoor in spots) On-property and connected resorts; shortest path to Caesars Forum and Expo halls Highest during conference week Central Strip (Bellagio–Paris cluster) 5–12 minutes walking or official shuttle Bellagio, Caesars Palace, Paris Las Vegas, The LINQ — official conference hotels with shuttle service[3] High with official block rates via housing portal North Strip (Wynn/Resorts World) 10–18 minutes walking or shuttle Encore, Wynn, Resorts World properties; quieter rooms, still on shuttle routes[3] Moderate to high with better availability when central blocks fill up The Venetian campus minimizes morning friction for keynotes and Expo appointments. Central Strip hotels trade a short walk or shuttle ride for dining along Las Vegas Boulevard. Properties on the North Strip work when official blocks sell out, but confirm shuttle eligibility before you book a hotel farther away from the Expo Center campus. Workday Rising hotel pricing October falls within Las Vegas's lower federal lodging tier, but a flagship enterprise conference still drives demand around the Venetian Expo Center. Hotels within walking distance often sell out or raise rates as the event approaches, so it's worth comparing conference hotel blocks with current market prices before you book. Navan analyzed anonymized hotel booking patterns near the Venetian Expo Center during October 2025 — the most recent October conference week in Navan booking data. Although Workday Rising is making its debut in Las Vegas for 2026, these figures provide a useful benchmark for conference-week pricing on the Strip.[16] Median hotel rate: During conference week, the median nightly rate near the venue was $329 — about 60% higher than a typical October week in the same area (median of $206). Stay length: Business travelers stayed an average of 2.8 nights. Check-in pattern: Monday was the most common arrival day, and Thursday the most common departure day. Late bookings: Roughly 36% of bookings were made within two weeks of check-in. What stands out: According to Navan data, travelers who booked 1–2 months before check-in paid a median of $286 per night, while waiting until the final 1–2 weeks pushed the median to $360.[16] That's a difference of about $74 per night, making early booking a safer strategy. Workday Rising flight trends The main airport serving Workday Rising attendees is Harry Reid International Airport (LAS). Navan flight data from a comparable October 2025 Las Vegas conference week shows 3,691 business flights into the city, with nearly 10% arriving from international destinations.[16] The busiest origin cities were San Francisco, New York, London, Newark, and Boston. Consider arriving a day early, to give yourself time to settle into your hotel, pick up your badge, and ease into the week. You'll start Monday focused on the conference instead of worrying about flight delays, luggage, or racing across the Strip. It searches based on the amenities you need , then it can book your flight, hotel, and restaurant reservations without sending you across multiple apps. If your plans change, you can get help comparing nearby alternatives, adjusting your itinerary, or handling unexpected travel disruptions, all in the same thread, with human travel experts on-call to enter the same chat upon request. The Loyalty Wallet keeps your program statuses and progress (including air miles) in one place for easy visibility. For a deeper look at the mechanics, see our guide on how to earn travel rewards on business trips . Set a realistic budget for Las Vegas before you go Your conference pass is only one part of the cost of attending Workday Rising. Budget for conference-week hotel rates, meals outside conference programming, airport transportation, client dinners, and other business travel expenses before you book. GSA per diem for Las Vegas The U.S. General Services Administration (GSA) sets federal per diem rates by city and season. At the time of publication, the following FY2026 rates apply to Las Vegas: $212 per day: Includes $126 per night for lodging and $86 per day for meals and incidental expenses (M&IE) M&IE breakdown: $21 for breakfast, $23 for lunch, $36 for dinner, and $6 for incidentals (deduct conference-provided meals from your meal claim as applicable) First and last travel days: M&IE is typically reimbursed at 75% of the daily rate ($64.50) when you're in transit Updated FY2027 (October 2026–September 2027) rates will be published in mid-August 2026, so verify the current figures at gsa.gov before traveling.[7] Conference-week hotel rates within walking distance of the Venetian Expo Center often exceed the federal lodging cap. Navan booking data from a comparable October 2025 Las Vegas conference week showed a median nightly rate of $329 near the venue — more than $200 above the FY2026 GSA lodging rate of $126.[16] Budget for that difference or consider staying farther along the Strip and using the official conference shuttles. Other budget considerations Before you travel, estimate your daily spending so there are fewer surprises when it's time to submit your expense report. Conference registration: Full Experience Passes start at $2,395; verify current pricing at rising.workday.com before registering.[8] Conference-provided meals: Registration includes the Welcome Reception, breakfast bites and lunch on Oct. 13–14, the Customer Appreciation Party, and brunch on Oct. 15. Adjust your meal reimbursement accordingly.[3] Airport transportation: Taxi fares to The Venetian are roughly $29 plus the airport pickup fee, while rideshares typically cost $15–$40 depending on demand and surge pricing.[9][10] Client dinners: Restaurants on the Strip commonly run $85–$200 per person for business dinners. After-hours networking: Partner receptions, team outings, and other unofficial events can add to your travel budget beyond the meals included with registration. Plan your Workday Rising 2026 agenda The Workday Rising 2026 Session Catalog is now available, giving attendees time to explore keynotes, breakouts, Hands-On Labs, and networking events before the conference begins.[1][17][18] Once the Session Scheduler opens in September, you'll be able to build your personal agenda and reserve eligible sessions.[1][3] Monday, Oct. 12: Welcome Reception, Welcome Keynote, and Workday Pro certifications Tuesday, Oct. 13: Innovation Keynote, Hands-On Labs, expert-led sessions, and peer networking Wednesday, Oct. 14: Customer stories, community breakouts, and the Customer Appreciation Party Thursday, Oct. 15: Expert meetups, networking, and closing sessions focused on applying what you've learned Featured speakers include Workday CEO Aneel Bhusri, President of Product and Technology Gerrit Kazmaier, and Chief AI Officer Joel Hellermark. Build flexibility into your schedule Start by browsing the Session Catalog and identifying your highest-priority sessions.[18] When the Session Scheduler opens in September, finalize your agenda and reserve popular labs before they fill. As you prepare for the conference: Sessions: Short-list must-attend sessions now, then reserve eligible labs and workshops once the Session Scheduler opens. Meetings: Reach out to customers, partners, or colleagues about two weeks before the conference to schedule short meetings while everyone is in one place. Logistics: Download the Workday Rising app, enable session alerts, set your out-of-office message, and save the Venetian Expo Center in your maps app. Networking: Decide how you'll exchange contact information and add a quick note after each conversation to make follow-up easier. For more tips on getting prepared for your trip, read our business trip planning guide covering flights, hotels, and departure checklists. What to pack and wear at Workday Rising Workday Rising calls for business casual: collared shirts or polished blouses, slacks or chinos, comfortable closed-toe shoes, and a light layer for over-air-conditioned ballrooms. Presenters and client-dinner hosts often dress one notch sharper, and Expo-floor browsing is more relaxed.[3] Las Vegas in October runs warm in the afternoon with highs around 85°F (29°C) and nights that can dip to 55°F (13°C).[3] You'll move between climate-controlled halls and outdoor Strip walks, so pack breathable daytime fabrics and a sweater or blazer for evening events. Conference essentials Everyone remembers their computer and charger, but don't forget to bring these must-pack items: Two pairs of comfortable shoes: Convention flooring and Strip distances punish single-shoe days. Portable charger: Session Scheduler, Braindate notes, and badge scans drain batteries by mid-afternoon. Snacks: Pack a few protein bars or other easy snacks for the gaps between sessions, long Expo visits, or client meetings that run through lunch. Reusable water bottle: Desert air dehydrates faster than you notice between sessions. Throat lozenges and hand sanitizer: Crowded keynotes and Expo aisles add up over four days. Light layer: Breakout rooms run cold even when the Strip is warm. Sunscreen: Outdoor walks between properties add up under strong afternoon sun. Getting from the airport to the Workday Rising venue Harry Reid International Airport (LAS) is about 3–5 miles from The Venetian Resort, making it one of the easier airport-to-conference transfers you'll find in Las Vegas.[9] Decide how you'll get to your hotel before you land so you can head straight to check-in. If your schedule allows, arrive on Oct. 11 to have time to check into your hotel, pick up your badge, and settle in before Monday's sessions and Welcome Reception. Navan Edge specialists can request an early check-in if needed. Option Time Cost Notes Taxi (zone rate) 15–25 minutes Around $29 + $2.40 airport fee[10] Curbside pickup with flat Strip zone pricing Rideshare (Uber/Lyft) 15–25 minutes $15–$40[9] Parking garage pickup with surge pricing during peak hours RTC Deuce bus 45–60 minutes Around $6[11] Best budget option if staying near a Strip stop Shared shuttle (third-party) 30–60 minutes $15–$19 per person Lower-cost rides if you don't mind multiple hotel stops For most business travelers, a taxi or rideshare is the quickest and easiest way to reach the Venetian, especially if you're traveling with luggage. The RTC Deuce is a reasonable option if you're staying near one of its stops and don't mind a longer trip. Beyond sessions: Make time for the Expo and networking Some of the most valuable conversations at Workday Rising happen outside the breakout rooms. Leave time to explore the Expo, attend product demonstrations, and connect with other attendees between sessions. Workday Rising Expo: Explore sponsor booths, product demonstrations, and innovation showcases throughout the Venetian Expo Center.[1][6] Braindates: Join peer-led discussions with other attendees to exchange ideas and compare experiences; reservations open with the Session Scheduler in September.[3] Hands-On Labs and Express Labs: Try new features in guided or drop-in technical sessions led by Workday experts.[3] Meetups and product demos: Take advantage of smaller sessions and informal conversations between keynotes and breakouts.[3] Session reservations: Some sessions require advance reservations, while others are first come, first served; check the Session Scheduler for details when it opens.[3] Make networking part of your plan A few thoughtful conversations can be more valuable than squeezing in one more breakout session. Before you travel: Make a short list of customers, partners, colleagues, or peers you'd like to meet, and reach out about two weeks before the conference to schedule time together. During the conference: After each conversation, jot down a quick note about what you discussed and any agreed-upon next steps. You'll thank yourself when it's time to follow up. At the end of each day: Spend a few minutes drafting follow-up emails while the conversations are still fresh, then send them within a day or two of returning home. Finally, leave yourself some breathing room. A packed agenda looks productive on paper, but a short break between sessions often leaves you with more energy for the conversations and ideas you'll remember long after the conference ends. What to eat at Workday Rising 2026 Workday provides meals throughout the conference — from the Welcome Reception and breakfast bites to conference lunches, the Customer Appreciation Party, and the closing brunch — so you're not paying for every meal on the Strip.[3] Client dinners and team outings usually fill the remaining gaps. For sit-down meals outside the venue, try these options on the Strip: Client dinner: Delmonico Steakhouse at The Venetian handles executive dinners with private rooms and classic steakhouse service steps from the Expo halls.[12] Team meal: Fogo de Chão in the Grand Canal Shoppes works for group dining with Brazilian table service and private rooms for larger teams.[13] Private dining / executive lunch: Cañonita near the Venetian Expo Center offers private and semi-private rooms for groups of 10–250 with customizable menus.[14] One-on-one or small group: Sugarcane on Restaurant Row is great for intimate meetings, thanks to its dedicated private dining room near the convention center.[15] If a six-person partner dinner is needed mid-week, Navan Edge can reserve Las Vegas restaurants in the same chat as your hotel and LAS flights. Finish strong on departure day Your time at Workday Rising isn't over until you're through LAS and back to your normal day-to-day work. Here's what to do before checkout: Pack the night before: Charge your gear, lay out your travel clothes, check the room for swag, chargers, and anything else you may have left behind. Confirm late checkout: Whether or not you remembered to request late checkout when checking in, check with the front desk or have Navan Edge coordinate on your behalf. Arrive early at the airport: After the conference you can expect long lines at LAS, so allow at least two hours for domestic flights and three hours for international. Submit expenses early: Upload receipts before your time at the symposium blurs together, and flag lodging above your per-diem cap when you file. Visit the airport lounge: Get quiet time to sort notes and receipts before boarding if your airline ticket includes lounge access. Calendar a debrief: Reserve an hour to message new contacts and summarize conference outcomes before regular work resumes. Make your Workday Rising 2026 trip count Workday Rising 2026 rewards attendees who arrive with a plan. Book the right hotel, set a realistic budget, prioritize the sessions that matter most, and leave room for the Expo and networking. Those choices make it easier to head home with stronger connections, clearer priorities, and ideas you can put into practice right away. Heading to Workday Rising 2026? title: Building for XREAL AURA: Inside Google's First Android XR Hackathon
summary: At Google's first Android XR hackathon 19 teams built for XREAL AURA in two days, and four of five finalists chose Unity. See who won and why.
body_text: Recently, Unity announced support for XREAL AURA , new wired XR glasses coming soon to Google’s Android XR ecosystem. Check out our docs to start building today, and watch our livestream featuring Google and XREAL! Last month, the XR industry got an exciting early look at what's coming this fall when Google hosted their first-ever Android XR hackathon, organized around building for XREAL AURA. Unity sponsored the event, and we sent a cross-functional team to be right in the middle of it: walking the floor, supporting developers in real time, cheering on the pitches, and carrying that energy into AWE the following week. Here's what we saw — and what got us excited. Two Days Building for XREAL AURA Over two packed days (June 13–14), 19 teams competed to build something brand new or port existing experiences to XREAL AURA. The crowd was a mix of backgrounds — students from universities like USC and Northeastern University rubbing shoulders with seasoned XR professionals who've been building in this space for years, if not decades. By the end of day two, every team stepped up to give a short demo and pitch to the judges. The energy in the room was alive with excitement to see which top 5 teams would win. Hackathon participants working on their projects Why Developers Chose Unity for Android XR Unsurprisingly, Unity was the popular choice — and the reasoning was straightforward. Developers who already knew Unity saw no reason to switch for a two-day sprint. When we spoke with developers, the phrase "it just works" came up more than once. Plus, teams with existing Unity XR codebases found porting surprisingly smooth once they dialed in their OpenXR settings . A few Made With Unity studios had even started porting their titles from Meta Quest and other platforms before the event — before receiving a developer kit. Why Some Developers Went a Different Route Not everyone reached for Unity, and those choices were thoughtful: Native / Jetpack was the go-to for teams building non-3D, window-based, or system-integrated apps. They wanted to stay close to the hardware — and in one fun case, a developer with a Unity background chose Jetpack purely because they wanted to learn something new. StereoKit came up for a developer who needed to modify engine source code directly — a real limitation of Unity's closed-source model for those doing deep hardware work. Healthcare, Robotics, and XR Newcomers A few things stood out as we talked to teams throughout the event: Healthcare and medical showed up strong. Multiple teams were building accessibility or healthcare-adjacent experiences — serious, enterprise-grade stuff that leans on Unity's stability. Robotics is finding a home in XR. Students from Northeastern University showed us a video demonstration of operators remotely controlling robots by manipulating a digital twin in XR — a compelling glimpse at how spatial computing could reshape human-robot interaction. First-timers were in the building: one team had never built an XR app before the hackathon, which is a meaningful signal — both Unity and XREAL AURA's approachability is pulling in entirely new developers, not just the veterans. Hackathon participants using the XREAL AURA glasses The Winners From 19 competing teams, judges representing Unity, Google, and the event's sponsors picked a top 5 — and one overall winner. Four of the five finalists built with Unity — a great reflection of where the ecosystem stands. Hackathon winners received Unity-branded swag and GCP credits. 🥇 Network XR (Overall Winner) created by Maksym Nesmashnyi, Horacio Torrendell, Jayasri Guthula, Ashray Pai, and Raydelto Hernandez: A conference networking platform using real-time face recognition to surface attendee profiles, shared interests, and conversation starters, with follow-up summaries generated on a web platform. Built with Unity + a Python backend. 🏅 Spatial Sailors created by Harold Serrano, Rodney White, and Adam Cooper: A 1v1 real-time naval strategy game with tactical and spatial elements. Built with Unity. 🏅 GastroSphere created by Moaz Sial, Oz Guvenc, Avinash Bolleddula, and Edmund: A clinical spatial computing platform that converts 2D medical imaging into interactive 3D anatomical models, powered by an offline multi-agent AI pipeline. Built with Jetpack Compose XR and Unity. 🏅 One Man Band created by Nick Suda, Stephen Rogers, Ian MacKenzie, and AJ Atkins: A live looping and jamming system with hand-tracked instruments, live sequencing, and a "ghost player" history recording feature. Built with Unity. 🏅 XR-Tract created by Philippe Lewicki, Jeff Breugelmans, and Ali Daniali: A reality-to-reality asset pipeline that captures real-world objects and converts them to game-ready 3D assets via cloud AI. Built with Godot. Unity swag for the winning teams Unity's Momentum Heading Into XREAL AURA Launch Unity’s support for Android XR and XREAL AURA has real momentum as the wired glasses head into their Fall 2026 retail launch. The developer community is engaged and energized, Unity is well-represented across the ecosystem, and the range of projects on display — from multiplayer games to enterprise tools to healthcare applications — shows a platform attracting serious builders. We left the hackathon genuinely excited about what's ahead.

title: Inbox Placement Rate: A Guide to Reaching the Primary Inbox
summary: Confused by your inbox placement rate? Learn how to measure it, what factors impact it, and the steps to take to avoid the spam and promotions folder for good.
body_text: Inbox placement rate is the percentage of emails that land in the recipient's main inbox, not the spam or promotions folder. The global average inbox placement rate fell below 85% in 2022, which means more than 15 out of every 100 emails sent were filtered into spam or junk folders, according to Validity's 2023 Email Deliverability Benchmark Report . That number changes how email performance should be judged. A campaign can look fine in a sending dashboard and still miss the place where people make decisions. For founders, sales teams, agencies, recruiters, and marketers, that's the difference between “sent” and “seen.” It's also why inbox placement rate matters more than surface metrics when email is tied to pipeline, bookings, hiring, or retention. What Is Inbox Placement Rate and Why It Matters Now Inbox placement rate is the percentage of emails that reach the recipient's primary inbox . It doesn't count server acceptance alone, and it doesn't treat the Promotions tab as equal to the main inbox. Why this metric matters more than delivery Many teams still look at “delivered” as if it means “visible.” It doesn't. According to Validity's 2023 Email Deliverability Benchmark Report , the global average inbox placement rate fell below 85% in 2022, meaning more than 15 out of every 100 emails sent were filtered into spam or junk folders. That's a major loss before the recipient even decides whether to open or reply. A business can write strong copy, target the right people, and still underperform if mailbox providers don't trust the sender. That's why inbox placement rate is closer to a truth metric than open rate or raw delivery rate. Practical rule: If email is a growth channel, the real question isn't “Did the server accept it?” It's “Did a human see it in the main inbox?” Why business owners should care now Mailbox providers have become stricter. They weigh trust, technical setup, recipient behavior, and complaint risk more heavily than many teams expect. That creates a real business problem. Cold outreach gets buried. Product emails lose visibility. Recruitment outreach misses candidates. Marketing campaigns look weaker than they really are. For teams improving outbound systems, list quality, and targeting, it also helps to pair deliverability work with broader valuable lead generation insights so better inbox placement translates into better pipeline, not just better diagnostics. Delivery vs Deliverability vs Inbox Placement These three terms get mixed together all the time. That confusion leads to bad decisions. A simple way to think about it is physical mail. Delivery means the building accepted the package. Deliverability means it wasn't rejected at the door. Inbox placement means it arrived at the recipient's desk instead of getting tossed into a side room. What each metric really measures Technically, Data Innovation explains that delivery rate confirms an email was accepted by the receiving server, while inbox placement rate measures what percentage of those delivered emails successfully bypass spam filters to reach the primary inbox, a metric that directly correlates with opens and conversions. That difference matters because accepted mail can still disappear into spam, junk, or secondary tabs. A “healthy” delivery rate can hide a weak campaign if placement is poor. Metric What It Measures Good Benchmark Delivery rate Whether the receiving server accepted the email Often judged by whether mail is consistently accepted, but this alone doesn't confirm visibility Deliverability Whether emails avoid outright rejection and broadly reach recipient systems Strong when authentication, reputation, and list quality keep rejection and filtering low Inbox placement Whether messages land in the primary inbox where people are likely to see them A strong inbox placement rate is above 85% in the primary inbox with less than 5% landing in spam, according to Data Innovation's benchmark guide Why teams optimize the wrong thing A lot of tools report what's easiest to measure, not what matters most. Server acceptance is easy. Primary inbox visibility is harder. That's why teams can feel confident while performance slips. If a sending platform says messages were delivered, it sounds like success. But the recipient may never see them. Three common mistakes show up here: Chasing acceptance only: Teams celebrate a high delivery rate while ignoring placement by provider. Ignoring authentication gaps: Broken alignment can let mail through but still weaken trust signals. A practical primer on this sits in Mailwarm's guide to mastering email authentication . Treating all inbox folders the same: Primary, Promotions, and spam don't drive the same business outcome. Delivery is a transport metric. Inbox placement is an attention metric. What Is a Good Inbox Placement Rate by Provider Provider averages tell a harder story than account-level dashboards. The same sender can perform well at one mailbox provider and badly at another. Why overall averages hide the real problem Provider-level data shows how misleading blended reporting can be. According to Mailmend's provider breakdown , Gmail may show a 95.54% deliverability rate , yet only 57.8% of messages land in the primary inbox. Consumer Microsoft accounts are even tougher, with inbox placement at 26.77% . That gap changes how senders should evaluate performance. A campaign can look stable in aggregate while one major provider suppresses most of the traffic. What counts as strong and weak placement Benchmarks are useful, but only if they're interpreted correctly. According to OIMetrics , a healthy inbox placement rate benchmark for strong email programs is 95% or higher , with delivery rates typically around 98–99% and spam complaint rates below 0.1% . Separately, Data Innovation defines a strong inbox placement rate as exceeding 85% in the primary inbox, with less than 5% landing in spam, while rates below 70% indicate poor sender reputation requiring immediate remediation. Those two views are useful together. One sets a high operating target. The other gives a practical threshold for diagnosing trouble. Why provider-level monitoring matters A sender shouldn't ask, “What's the inbox placement rate?” The better question is, “What's the inbox placement rate at Gmail, Outlook, Microsoft 365, Yahoo, and the providers that matter most to this audience?” That's especially important in B2B. A team selling into Microsoft-heavy organizations can't rely on blended averages if Outlook-family placement is weak. A practical review should include: Provider splits: Separate Gmail from Microsoft traffic. Primary inbox focus: Don't count Promotions as equivalent visibility. Trend monitoring: Look for drift, not just snapshots. The Four Pillars of High Inbox Placement Inbox placement improves when the fundamentals line up. The work usually falls into four buckets: authentication, reputation, engagement, and content discipline. Authentication proves the sender is real Mailbox providers want proof that the sender is who they claim to be. According to MessageFlow's deliverability guide , the most decisive signals now include strong authentication through SPF, DKIM, and DMARC , spam complaint rates below 0.1% , bounce rates below 2% , and positive engagement signals like replies. For teams that want a practical outside explanation of setup logic, this walkthrough on email authentication for personalized campaigns is a useful reference. Reputation determines how much trust the sender has earned Reputation is the long-term score mailbox providers build from behavior. It's tied to the sending domain, infrastructure, complaint patterns, bounce patterns, and recipient response. A sender with unstable habits usually sees placement drift. That includes sudden volume spikes, poor list quality, or repeated sends to disengaged contacts. Useful checks include: Complaint control: Keep complaint pressure low. Bounce prevention: Remove invalid addresses early. Consistency: Increase volume gradually, not abruptly. Engagement tells providers whether recipients value the email Many teams often underestimate this problem. Mailbox providers don't just inspect the sender. They also watch what recipients do. Signals that tend to help include: Replies: They're among the strongest positive signals. Threads and ongoing interaction: They suggest a real relationship. Spam removal and important marking: They reinforce legitimacy. A technically correct email can still underperform if recipients ignore it. Content quality supports the other three pillars Content alone won't rescue a weak sender reputation, but weak content can absolutely make a good setup worse. The goal isn't to “beat filters” with tricks. The goal is to send mail that matches recipient intent, reads like human communication, and doesn't trigger avoidable suspicion. A practical checklist helps: Keep relevance high: Send to people who should receive the message. Keep formatting clean: Overdesigned or noisy messages often work against trust. Keep segmentation tight: Don't send the same message to active and stale contacts. For a practical checklist on reducing filtering risk, Mailwarm's guide on how to avoid the spam folder is useful reading. Your Playbook to Monitor and Improve Inbox Placement Inbox placement doesn't improve by guessing. It improves through measurement, cleanup, gradual reputation building, and ongoing review. A practical workflow starts with visibility. Step 1: Test placement before changing anything According to Litmus , measuring inbox placement rate effectively requires a seed list of test addresses across major providers like Gmail and Outlook. That helps detect reputation drift, where a sender might see 95% placement at Yahoo but only 60% at Outlook because filtering algorithms differ by provider. That kind of test is often the fastest way to stop arguing with misleading dashboard metrics. For teams that want a quick external check, MailGenius offers a free inbox placement test . Step 2: Fix the technical layer If authentication is misaligned or incomplete, everything else becomes harder. Before touching copy, review the sending setup, return-path alignment, and reputation basics. The goal here is simple: Confirm authentication is working Review bounce and complaint patterns Separate sending streams when needed Stop sending to clearly stale or risky segments Step 3: Warm up with realistic engagement New domains, newly activated mailboxes, and underused senders usually need a gradual trust-building phase. That's where a lot of teams make the wrong trade-off and rely on shallow automation. It uses 50,000+ aged real inboxes , supports provider-level warmup, tracks spam score and placement signals, offers custom content warmup, includes authentication fix tools and bounce prevention, and doesn't require IMAP access or permission to read a user's private inbox. Expert deliverability calls are included in every plan. The key idea isn't “more warmup activity.” It's better trust signals. Step 4: Improve the message and the audience If placement is unstable, the audience often needs as much work as the copy. Good habits include: Trim cold segments: Don't keep mailing people who never engage. Match the message to the segment: Generic outreach creates weak interaction signals. Ask for simple engagement: Replies matter more than vanity activity. A useful training resource on this topic is included below. Step 5: Monitor by provider and keep adjusting Inbox placement isn't static. Sender reputation shifts over time, especially after changes in volume, targeting, or list quality. A practical monitoring routine should track: Provider-level results Primary vs secondary tab behavior Spam complaints Bounce trends Engagement quality, especially replies Teams that review this weekly catch problems much earlier than teams that wait for a campaign collapse. Why Basic Warmup Fails to Improve Real Inbox Placement Basic warmup often focuses on easy signals. The problem is that mailbox providers care more about believable signals. The Promotions tab is not the same as the primary inbox A lot of warmup discussions flatten the outcome into “inbox vs spam.” That's too simplistic for businesses that need replies, meetings, and real action. According to BulkEmailChecker , 30-40% of delivered cold emails land in the Promotions tab, and that can reduce reply rates by half despite technically good inbox placement. The same source notes that real engagement, especially replies, is the top factor for achieving Primary placement. That changes what “success” means. If a campaign reaches Promotions instead of Primary, it may be technically delivered and still commercially weak. Why automated activity alone falls short Many basic tools generate activity that looks repetitive or thin. Opens without meaningful interaction don't carry the same weight as replies, threads, removals from spam, or important marking. That's why teams often see a short-lived bump and then plateau. The sender is producing motion, but not enough trust. A better standard for evaluating any warmup system is: Does it create realistic engagement? body_text: Most email enrichment tools fall into one of two traps. Either they're bloated all-in-one platforms that charge enterprise prices for features you'll never use, or they're cheap but unreliable, filling your pipeline with bounced emails and wasted outreach. For AI agents running outbound workflows, neither option works. Agents need accurate data, fast APIs, and economics that don't blow through budgets on verification alone. Today we're excited to announce our partnership with Icypeas , a specialist email enrichment platform trusted by Clay, Lemlist, Apollo, Instantly, LaGrowthMachine, and PhantomBuster. Icypeas focuses on doing a few things exceptionally well: finding professional emails, verifying them, scanning domains, and searching people and company databases. Their email discovery delivers the lowest bounce rate on the market with one of the highest find rates, and they do it at 3 to 10x cheaper than Wiza, Findymail, and Dropcontact. What is Icypeas? Icypeas is a B2B email enrichment platform built for sales, marketing, and GTM teams who need reliable contact data without paying for a bloated suite. Founded by Pierre Landoin, who brings over 10 years of lead generation expertise, Icypeas takes the specialist approach: a focused set of features that outperform generalist alternatives. Their core products: Email Finder : Find professional email addresses from a person's first name, last name, and company domain. Returns emails with confidence scores (ultra_sure, very_sure, probable, risky) and MX provider detection. Email Verification : Verify whether an email address exists and is deliverable. Catches invalid, disposable, and catch-all addresses before they bounce. Domain Scan : Discover all role-based email addresses for a domain (support@, sales@, info@, hr@). Useful for finding the right team to contact at any organization. People Search : Search a database of professionals by job title, seniority, company size, location, and more. Returns contact details at 0.02 credits per result. Company Search : Search companies by industry, employee count, address, keywords, and domain. Build target account lists programmatically. LinkedIn Profile Scraping : Scrape full LinkedIn profiles including work history, education, headline, and contact info. LinkedIn Company Scraping : Get employee count, industry, revenue, growth metrics, founded year, and address for any LinkedIn company page. Reverse Email Lookup : Find the LinkedIn profile URL behind any professional email address. Bulk Search : Run up to 5,000 email searches, verifications, or domain scans in a single API call with webhook notifications on completion. title: Payment Terms: Meaning, Types, Examples & Best Practices
summary: Understand payment terms with simple examples, invoice formats, common payment conditions, MSME and export payment terms, and digital payment best practices.
body_text: Table of Contents Toggle Every invoice has a due date, but getting paid on time depends on much more than that. Payment terms help businesses clearly define when customers should pay, which payment methods are accepted, whether early payment discounts apply, and what happens if payments are delayed. For MSMEs, freelancers, SaaS businesses, exporters, and enterprises, well-defined payment terms improve cash flow, reduce payment disputes, and create better customer relationships. 📌 Key Takeaways Payment terms define when, how, and under what conditions customers should pay. Common payment terms include Due on Receipt, Net 15, Net 30, Net 60, Advance Payment, Cash on Delivery (COD), and Milestone Payments. Clear payment terms help businesses improve cash flow, reduce payment disputes, and set clear payment expectations. Offering digital payment methods like UPI, Cards, Payment Links, and Net Banking makes it easier for customers to pay on time. Export businesses commonly use payment terms such as Advance Payment, Letter of Credit (LC), Documents Against Payment (D/P), Documents Against Acceptance (D/A), and Open Account. What Are Payment Terms? Payment terms are the agreed conditions that define when and how a customer should pay for goods or services. They specify payment deadlines, accepted payment methods, discounts for early payment, penalties for late payment, and any other conditions agreed upon between the buyer and seller. You’ll typically find payment terms on invoices, purchase orders, quotations, and contracts. In simple terms, payment terms answer three important questions: When should the customer pay? How should they pay? What happens if they pay early or late? Example A business issues an invoice worth ₹100,000 with Net 30 payment terms. This means the customer must pay the full invoice amount within 30 days from the invoice date . Payment Terms vs Payment Conditions While these terms are often used together, they cover different aspects of a transaction. Component What It Covers Payment Terms Due date, payment schedule, credit period Payment Conditions Accepted payment methods, discounts, penalties, taxes, currency, milestone payments, and special requirements Together, they define the complete payment agreement between buyer and seller. What Do Payment Terms and Conditions Include? Payment terms often include several important elements, such as: Payment due date (Due on Receipt, Net 15, Net 30, etc.) Accepted payment methods ( UPI , Cards, Net Banking, Wallets, Bank Transfer) Early payment discounts (for example, 2/10 Net 30 ) Late payment charges or interest Partial payment or milestone schedules Currency (especially for international invoices) Applicable taxes and GST Invoice reference or purchase order details Clearly written payment terms help businesses reduce payment disputes , accelerate collections, and improve cash flow predictability. Common Types of Payment Terms Different businesses use different payment terms depending on their industry, customer relationships, and cash flow requirements. Payment Term Meaning Best For Due on Receipt Payment is due immediately after receiving the invoice Retail, Freelancers, D2C Net 15 Payment due within 15 days MSMEs Net 30 Payment due within 30 days B2B Businesses Net 60 Payment due within 60 days Large Enterprises Advance Payment Customer pays partially or fully before work begins Manufacturing, Custom Orders Cash on Delivery (COD) Payment collected when goods are delivered Ecommerce Milestone Payment Payments released after completing project phases Agencies, Contractors 2/10 Net 30 2% discount if paid within 10 days; otherwise due in 30 days B2B Sales Businesses choose payment terms based on customer creditworthiness, negotiation power, project size, and working capital needs. Payment Terms for MSMEs in India For MSMEs , payment terms have a direct impact on working capital . Since many small businesses purchase raw materials or pay employees before receiving customer payments, delayed collections can create serious cash flow challenges. Some commonly used payment terms for MSMEs include: 50% advance and 50% on delivery Net 7, Net 15, or Net 21 instead of longer credit periods Milestone-based payments for projects and services Early payment discounts to encourage faster collections Under the MSMED Act , eligible MSMEs are protected against delayed payments, and buyers may be liable to pay interest on overdue invoices in certain situations. Clearly mentioning payment terms on invoices helps businesses strengthen payment discipline and reduce disputes. Offering customers convenient payment options like UPI, cards, payment links , and bank transfers further improves the chances of receiving payments on time. Example: MSME Invoice Payment Terms A small manufacturing MSME supplies machine components to a larger company. The invoice includes: Payment Terms: 30% advance, remaining 70% payable within 15 days of delivery (Net 15) Payment Methods: UPI, Cards, Net Banking, Payment Link Late Fee: 1.5% per month on overdue payments The advance payment covers raw material costs, while the shorter credit period improves working capital and reduces outstanding receivables. Export Payment Terms International transactions involve additional risks such as currency fluctuations, longer shipping timelines, and cross-border compliance. As a result, exporters and importers commonly use standardized payment terms that balance risk for both parties. Common export payment terms include: Advance Payment – Buyer pays before shipment. Letter of Credit (LC) – A bank guarantees payment once agreed documents are presented. Documents Against Payment (D/P) – Buyer pays before receiving shipping documents. Documents Against Acceptance (D/A) – Buyer accepts a time draft and pays later. Open Account – Goods are shipped first, with payment made on a future agreed date. The appropriate payment term depends on the level of trust between trading partners, transaction value, and country-specific risks. Example: Export Payment Terms An Indian apparel exporter ships garments to a buyer in Europe. The agreed payment terms are: 20% Advance Payment 80% payable through a Letter of Credit at Sight Currency: EUR Payment released after submitting shipping documents such as the commercial invoice, bill of lading, and packing list This structure provides upfront working capital while reducing payment risk through bank-backed assurance. Follow these best practices: Clearly mention payment due dates. Offer multiple payment methods . Keep payment instructions simple and easy to understand. Include late payment charges where applicable. Offer early payment discounts to encourage faster payments. Use milestone payments for long-term projects. Send automated payment reminders before due dates. Keep payment terms consistent across quotations, contracts, and invoices. Cashfree Payments helps businesses turn payment terms into seamless payment experiences by enabling them to: Share Payment Links or Pay Now buttons for immediate invoice payments. Accept payments through UPI, Cards, Net Banking, Wallets, and Pay Later from a single integration. Set up Subscriptions and Auto-Debits for recurring billing , SaaS subscriptions, EMIs, and retainers. Improve payment collection with faster digital checkout experiences and automated payment reminders. Track settlements and reconcile payments efficiently for better cash flow visibility. By combining clear invoice terms with digital payment infrastructure, businesses can reduce payment delays and improve overall collection efficiency. Good payment terms help businesses: Improve cash flow forecasting. Reduce payment disputes. Minimize overdue invoices. Strengthen customer relationships. Support better inventory and working capital planning. Encourage faster payments through discounts and convenient digital payment methods. For MSMEs, exporters, freelancers, and growing businesses, the right payment terms can make a significant difference to financial stability. Conclusion Payment terms define when and how customers pay for goods or services, making them a critical part of every invoice, contract, and business agreement. Whether you’re an MSME, freelancer, exporter, or enterprise, choosing the right payment terms helps improve cash flow, reduce payment delays, and create stronger customer relationships. When combined with digital payment solutions such as UPI, payment links, cards, subscriptions, and automated reminders, payment terms become more than contractual language, they become a practical way to get paid faster and manage business finances more efficiently.
